title: Adaptive castless attention kernel arbitration for mixed‑precision streaming
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement an arbitration layer that enables an attention execution path to avoid runtime cast/dequant cycles where possible ("castless"), switching between INT8, FP8 and FP16/WebFloat paths at lane granularity. The goal is to reduce per‑token dequant/requant overhead on streaming prefill+decode workloads while preserving accuracy and SLOs. This work touches kernel selection heuristics, attention tiling, KV cache memory layout, and scheduler admission policies.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end benchmark shows >=10% median tail latency reduction (p95) on streaming decode for BERT-style and transformer-decoder models on INT8-capable nodes compared to current mixed-precision baseline.
Token compute cost (GPU FLOP-equivalent) reduced by >=8% on representative production workloads without measurable quality regression (<=0.5% perplexity change / model-specific evals).
No regressions in existing prefilling correctness tests and all new castless-path unit tests pass in CI.
Fallbacks to existing dequantizing kernels are exercised and telemetry shows correct routing decisions under constrained capacity scenarios.
implementation_notes: Introduce a lightweight per-lane precision token in request metadata to allow scheduler to prefer castless lanes when KV layout and kernel availability permit.
Extend kernel-capability registry with tags: supports_castless_attention, int8_streaming_prefill, fp8_decode_fastpath.
Add an attention microkernel that operates on packed INT8 keys/queries & uses fused scale+softmax when scale factors are compatible; requires aligned KV packing to 128B lanes.
Scheduler: implement 'lane arbitration' that considers (a) current KV cache alignment, (b) model layer precision map, (c) latency credit for switching, (d) kernel health signals from telemetry.

Prefill/Decode overlap: attempt overlap of prefill decode for initial tokens when castless kernels can be reused to avoid round trips to dequant path. Use conservative heuristics for first rollout (no cross-tenant changes).
Instrumentation: emit decision_reason string for each routed request for debug/ops, and sampling of exec path + kernel_id in trace spans.
Compatibility: provide a config flag (runtime.experimental.castless_attention = true) and rollout via canary on dedicated pools before enabling for hosted API.
test_plan: Unit tests for kernel registry lookups and lane arbitration decisions (deterministic inputs).
Synthetic microbenchmarks: prefill-only, decode-only, and mixed streaming scenarios across sequence lengths 64/256/1024.
A/B rollouts on dedicated pool comparing baseline routing vs castless arbitration for 24h, capturing p50/p95 latency, token cost, and top-k quality metrics.
Regression tests: ensure identical logits shape and KV cache invariants across castless and fallback paths for a set of canonical prompts.
Chaos test: simulate kernel eviction and saturate lanes to verify fallback and no deadlocks.
risks: Castless kernels rely on stricter data alignment and packing; poor packing or fragmentation may cause throughput drop instead of improvement.
Numerical differences when skipping dequant/requant could surface small quality regressions on edge-case prompts; need prompt-set based evals.
Increased scheduler complexity could add overhead; must keep arbitration decision time < 50 microseconds on request path.
Rolling back incorrectly may be noisy — ensure opt-out config and automated canary monitors.
